_expect.name: Uncompahgre Gorge aka Ouray Ice Park

co_uncompahgre_gorge_aka_ouray_ice_park.blurb: A narrow, shaded canyon on the south edge of the town of Ouray in southwest Colorado, where irrigation water is sprayed down the walls each winter to grow ice curtains. Nearly all of the climbing is water ice, with a smaller set of mixed lines. WI4 is the most common grade, backed by plenty of WI3 and WI5 and a few easier WI2 and harder WI6 lines; the mixed climbs run from M5 up into the high M grades. A mile or two of gorge is split into many separate areas, from South Park at the far upstream end down past the Lower Bridge to the Scottish Gullies, with the Five Fingers area and School Room also well stocked. Ice is usually in from about mid-December to late March, and walking farther upstream tends to mean fewer people.

md_great_falls_maryland_side.blurb: Short cliffs and outcrops along the Maryland bank of the Potomac, in the river gorge below Great Falls. The gorge rock is mica schist, slick and poor at taking protection, so many climbers set up top ropes from anchors built around trees and boulders. Walls here run roughly 20 to 60 feet. Bouldering makes up more than half of the climbing, with problems from V0 to V6 forming the bulk and a thin tail above that, while the roped lines mostly sit between 5.8 and 5.11 and cluster around 5.10, with a few easier ones. Sub-areas include Purple Horse, Spitzbergen, Crag X and the Rocky Islands. Some outcrops sit right at the waterline, high water can cut off parts of the gorge, and the river itself deserves respect.

nm_dona_ana_mountains.blurb: A small, rugged desert range a few kilometers north of Las Cruces and just east of the Rio Grande, heavily eroded and mostly bare of vegetation. Most of the climbing is bouldering, with a smaller group of trad lines and only a couple of sport and top-rope routes. Boulder problems are weighted toward the easy end, V0 to V3 making up most of them, with a thinner run up into double-digit V grades; the roped climbs mostly fall between 5.8 and 5.10. Compared with the Organ Mountains the range is less dramatic, but approaches are shorter. Corkscrew Boulders and Pizza Boulders hold the most problems, and many Pizza Boulders problems face north, which can stretch the season into summer. Checkerboard Wall, a cliff of roughly 500 feet with several moderate lines, is the main roped objective.

nl_flatrock.blurb: Sea cliffs on the Atlantic side of the Avalon Peninsula, about half an hour north of St. John's. The rock is dense, vertical conglomerate sandstone, which makes gear placements tricky, and many trad lines carry bolts at the hard moves. Trad is the biggest share, followed by a solid block of sport routes and a good number of boulder problems. Roped grades stretch up to 5.13 but mostly sit between 5.9 and 5.12, and the problems are mostly V0 to V4 with a few much harder. The cliffs are modest in height and approaches are short. East-facing walls such as UV Ray and The Locker catch morning sun, while Blood Bath is a better afternoon choice, and Main Face holds the most routes. A steady sea breeze keeps bugs down, and whales and icebergs are often in view.

ca_malibu_creek_state_park.blurb: Canyon crags in the Santa Monica Mountains above the Malibu coast, cut into pocketed volcanic stone. Bolted sport routes dominate, with a sizeable group of top-rope lines and a handful of boulder problems. Grades are centered on 5.10 to 5.12, with a thinner spread of easier climbs and a few 5.13s. Main areas include Mt. Gorgeous, the Century Lake area and the Stumbling Blocks, while Planet of the Apes Wall is a popular top-rope wall. Reaching the main crags means a walk past the rock pool, where an easy traverse leads on to the walls, and the canyon feels more secluded the deeper you go. The creek and pool draw swimmers and hikers, so expect to share the canyon.

co_pool_of_plenty_boulder_area.blurb: A bouldering zone on Nine Mile Hill in Unaweep Canyon, south of Grand Junction in western Colorado, at roughly 5,900 feet. It spreads over a lot of ground with plenty of boulders; quality varies, though much of the rock is very solid. A few boulders sit in a secluded, oasis-like pocket with water, which gives this zone a different feel from other Nine Mile areas, and creekside landings can flood during spring runoff. Everything here is a boulder problem, mostly V1 to V4, with a few V5 and V6 and a handful of easier ones. The four main clusters are Moonshine, Rising Sun, Candy Store and Aqua, each holding dozens of problems.
